title: A tuning permission is not the selected kernel configuration
applies_when: A configuration-validation proposal interprets enable/allow flags as a forced execution path, especially when a separate knobs resolver or autotuner chooses the actual kernel policy. For FlashInfer MegaMoeConfig, trace enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce, combine_dtype and the resolved in_kernel_fc2_reduce separately.
lesson: Trace permission, resolved knobs and the consuming validator separately before adding an earlier rejection. FlashInfer NVFP4 MegaMoE allows enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=True while its default selector turns in_kernel_fc2_reduce off for mxfp8/nvfp4 combine wires and selects reuse_dispatch_warps. A constructor regression demanding rejection conflates permission with selection and can reject an existing permitted-but-unselected configuration. Test that control alongside explicitly incompatible selected knobs; inspect where the latter are already rejected.
avoid_when: An enable flag can be a mandatory execution choice in another API; establish its contract rather than applying this distinction universally. Explicit selected knobs can still be invalid. These pinned sources establish a default-selection counterexample, not all knob combinations, native kernel correctness, distributed reachability or performance. Inconsistent comments may warrant clarification without changing accepted inputs.

evidence.note: The outer config distinguishes permission from knobs that may disable the path. Its wire-format comment alone does not establish that every permitted session selects in-kernel reduction.
The actual default selector forces the selected reduction off for quantized combine wires, even when the caller granted permission.
The lower-level config rejects incompatible selected reduction, wire format and top-k policies before kernel construction. This is source evidence, not a native GPU qualification.
